title: What Does a Web Developer Actually Do?
description: A plain explanation of the job for people hiring one rather than becoming one: what the work involves, what it does not, and which kind you need.

blocks.v: Most explanations of this job are written for people who want to become a web developer. This one is written for the person who needs to hire one and is not sure what they are buying.

The confusion is reasonable. The title covers work that ranges from arranging text on a page to building the system that moves money between two banks. Two people can both call themselves web developers and share almost no skills.
The short version

A web developer writes the code that makes a website or web application work. A designer decides what it should look like and how it should behave. A developer makes that real, connects it to the things it needs to talk to, and keeps it running once people are using it.
If the designer draws the building, the developer builds it, runs the plumbing and wiring, and is the person you call when the lift stops.
Web development as a field covers both of those halves, and a third part nobody mentions at the quoting stage, which is keeping the thing alive after launch. All three are described below.
What the work actually involves
Turning a design into a working page

A design is a picture. The developer rebuilds it in code so it works at every screen size, loads quickly, responds to a keyboard as well as a mouse, and still reads correctly for someone using a screen reader. This part looks like the whole job from the outside. It is usually the smaller half.
Making it do something

A page that displays information is one problem. A page that does something is a different one. Search with filters, a form that produces a real enquiry, a booking flow, a calculator, a login, a payment. Each of these has rules, edge cases and failure states that nobody draws in the design.
This is where almost all project time and almost all cost actually goes.
Connecting it to everything else

Very few businesses want a website that stands alone. They want enquiries in their CRM, orders in their accounting system, listings pulled from a property feed, messages arriving on WhatsApp. Each connection depends on somebody else's system, their documentation and their uptime.
Keeping it working

Software decays. Browsers update, dependencies get security patches, the payment provider changes an endpoint, somebody uploads a 12MB photograph and the homepage takes nine seconds to load. A developer who disappears at launch has handed you a liability with a nice homepage.
What a web developer does not do
Worth knowing before you assume it is included:

v: Write your copy. Most developers will not, and the ones who offer to are often not the right person for it.
Decide what the site should say or who it is for. That is strategy, and it should be settled before anyone opens a code editor.
Design it, unless they specifically also design. Plenty do both. Plenty do not, and a developer-made layout usually looks like one.
Market it. Building a site and getting people to it are separate jobs with separate budgets.
Take the photographs. The single most common reason a finished build sits unlaunched is that nobody owns the images.

blocks.v: For a typical business website, full stack is the normal answer. For a product with real complexity on either side, two specialists beat one generalist.
Developer, engineer, programmer: does the word matter?
Not much, and anyone who tells you otherwise is describing a preference rather than a standard. There is no licensing body deciding who may use which title. Judge the work, not the noun.
The one distinction worth noticing is that "engineer" is sometimes used to signal systems and scale rather than websites. If your project is a brochure site, that signal is not relevant to you.
What this means when you are hiring
Three things decide whether you get a working asset or an expensive problem, and none of them is the day rate:

v: Can they explain the part that is hard about your project? A developer who says everything is straightforward has not thought about it.
Will you speak to the person writing the code? In an agency you often will not, and a brief loses detail at every handover.
What happens in month three? Ask who fixes a bug after launch and what it costs. The answer tells you whether you are buying a project or a relationship.

blocks.v: I have written a longer list of hiring questions separately, including the ownership questions most people forget to ask until it is too late to ask them.
Frequently asked questions
Do I need a web developer or a web designer?
If you need it to look right, a designer. If you need it to work, a developer. Most real projects need both, which is why many businesses hire one person who does both or an agency that supplies two.
Can one person build my whole website?

For most business websites, yes. A full stack developer who also designs can take a brochure site or a small application from nothing to launch. Past a certain complexity, one person becomes the bottleneck and a small team is faster.
How do I tell a good developer from a convincing one?

Ask to see something live that is still running, and ask what it does for that business. A portfolio of designs proves someone can present. A working site with real traffic behind it proves someone can finish.
What does a web developer cost in Dubai?

It depends far more on what you are building than on who builds it. My own published project minimum is AED 31,500 and retainers start at AED 16,000 a month, stated so there is one real number here rather than a range with nobody behind it. Those are my rates, not a market survey.
Published 4 October 2026 by a Dubai-based freelance developer. All AED figures are my own published rates.
